skills.title: Skills catalogue
skills.purpose: Every published skill, what it means at each level, who needs it now and in 2030, and how it maps to international frameworks.

skills-frameworks.title: International crosswalk
skills-frameworks.purpose: How Kafa'a skills map to ESCO, O*NET, SFIA 9, SkillsFuture, DigComp and other frameworks, with a machine-readable export.

skills-skill.title: Skill
skills-skill.purpose: Definition, level essence, roles now and in 2030, learning that builds it, crosswalk and sources.

admin-skills-alignments.title: Skills crosswalk editor
admin-skills-alignments.purpose: Add, edit, review and retire crosswalk rows. Framework owners edit; auditors read.

skills-rising.title: ENEC Skills on the Rise
skills-rising.purpose: The skills rising across ENEC this quarter: in demand now and growing, with the signals behind each one.

skills-rising-method.title: How Skills on the Rise is counted
skills-rising-method.purpose: The three signals, the thresholds and the suppression rule behind the quarterly list, the manager pulse and the technology badges.

workforce-skill-signals.title: Skill signal workbench
workforce-skill-signals.purpose: Compute and publish the quarterly list, read the manager pulse and the skill-suggestion counts as aggregates.

my-manager-pulse.title: Manager pulse
my-manager-pulse.purpose: Once a year, tell HR how much of your team's core skill set you expect to change by 2030.

skills-technologies.title: Technologies in demand
skills-technologies.purpose: Generic technologies that are hot across ENEC and the ones in demand for your role, with the counts behind each badge.

admin-skills-technologies.title: Technology tags and badges
admin-skills-technologies.purpose: Maintain the generic technology catalogue, tag opportunities and role profiles, and publish the quarterly badges.

my-skills-suggestions.title: Skills you may have
my-skills-suggestions.purpose: Skills inferred from your own work and learning. Confirm, reject or mark not me; nothing is added until you confirm.

exact.label: Exact
exact.help: Same meaning and scope: the external entry and the Kafa'a skill can be used interchangeably.

close.label: Close
close.help: Nearly the same: small differences in scope or wording.

broad.label: Broad
broad.help: The external entry is wider: the Kafa'a skill is one part of it.

partial.label: Partial
partial.help: Overlap only: some of the Kafa'a skill is covered, some is not.

match.indicativeNote: A row stays "indicative" until a second framework owner reviews it. Codes are stored only when copied from the framework's own source; otherwise the row is label-level and the code is pending review.

review.indicativeHelp: Not yet reviewed by a framework owner: use as a guide only.

levels.caption: Kafa'a level to external level
levels.none: No level map: this framework has no proficiency levels.

export.valid: The export validates against the CASE-shaped schema: {items} items, {assoc} associations.

explorer.intro: What each skill means at each level, which roles need it now and in 2030, what builds it, and how it maps to international frameworks. Search in English or Arabic.
explorer.searchPh: e.g. data analysis, تحليل البيانات, systems thinking
explorer.obsoleteHidden: {n} obsolete skill hidden; it stays reachable by link:
explorer.noHitsBody: Try another word, the Arabic or English name, or clear the filters.

why.name: Name contains your search: "{name}"
why.words: All {n} words appear in the name, labels or description

mine.signIn: Sign in to see your level for this skill and keep it as a goal.
mine.notHeld: Not in your skills passport yet.
mine.goalNote: Goals are private to you. Add a target date under "Skills I want to grow" to plan it and, if you choose, share it with your manager.
mine.securityNote: Security skills follow the security career path and are not personal goals.
mine.obsoleteNote: This skill is obsolete: add its replacement to your goals instead.
mine.planGoal: Add a target date (Skills I want to grow)

skill.noReplacement: No replacement: kept for the record.
skill.noDeployment: Awareness for planning only: no deployment decision implied.
skill.allFrameworks: See every framework and download the crosswalk
skill.ladder: What it means at each level
skill.ladderNote: The key level carries the skill's own essence line; each level lists the observable indicators published for this skill (FS23), or says why the skill is not defined there.
skill.noRoles: No published role profile asks for it at this horizon.
skill.rolesNote: From the published role profiles (FS05). 2030 and 2035 profiles are planning assumptions: no deployment decision or headcount implied.
skill.noLearningBody: Courses, pathways and credentials for future skills arrive in the next wave.

credVia.course: through a course that builds it

fw.intro: How each Kafa'a skill maps to international frameworks, so a profile, a course or a vacancy can be compared and exchanged. Codes are stored only when copied from the framework's own source; rows stay indicative until a second framework owner reviews them.
fw.tCoverageSub: {n} of {total} published skills have at least one alignment
fw.exportDesc: The published framework as a CASE-shaped package (1EdTech Competencies and Academic Standards Exchange) in the page language, and the crosswalk as CSV. Identifiers are stable between exports.
fw.registryDesc: Each framework, what Kafa'a uses from it, and how its codes and levels work.
fw.matrix: Coverage by framework and skill group
fw.matrixDesc: Skills with at least one published alignment, per framework and skill group.
fw.matrixNote: Cells show mapped skills out of the skills in that group; darker means more coverage.
fw.listDesc: Filter by framework, match type or review state.

admin.intro: Every crosswalk row with its status and review state. Framework owners add, edit, review and retire rows; every action is audited. Reviews follow maker-checker: never your own edit.
admin.readOnlyBody: Auditors read every row, including drafts and retired rows. Framework owners edit.
admin.reviewConsequence: The row stops showing "indicative" in English and Arabic. Your role and the date are recorded and audited.
admin.retireConsequence: It leaves the public crosswalk and the export, but is kept with your reason (never deleted).
admin.fCode: External code (only if copied from the source)
admin.codeHint: Format: {p}. Leave empty when you have not copied it.
admin.codeHintNone: Leave empty unless you copied the code from the source: the row then shows "code pending review".
admin.fArOfficial: The Arabic label comes from the framework itself
admin.fPublishHint: Unpublished rows stay drafts for framework owners.
admin.editNote: Saving an edit adds a version and makes the row indicative again until another framework owner reviews it.
admin.saveConsequence: The change is saved through the audited crosswalk RPC.

check.obsolete: This skill is obsolete: keep its existing alignments, but do not add new ones.
check.framework: Choose one of the listed frameworks.
check.label: Give the external label in English and Arabic (up to 200 characters each).
check.code: This code does not have the format the framework publishes. Leave it empty if you have not copied it from the source.
check.url: Cite the source with an https link.
check.as_of: Give the date you read the source (not in the future).
check.level_map: Each level-map entry takes up to 40 characters.
check.duplicate: This skill already has an active alignment to that framework entry.
check.immutable: The skill and framework of an alignment cannot change: retire it and add a new one.

aiTitle.literacy: Part of the AI fluency ladder (literacy)
aiTitle.engineering: AI engineering skill (specialists; not part of the literacy rung)

rs.not_signed_in: Sign in to see ENEC Skills on the Rise.
rs.forbidden: Your role cannot do this step of the Skills on the Rise workflow.
rs.invalid: Choose a quarter from 2025 Q1 to the current quarter.
rs.open_quarter: A quarter is published only after it has ended.
rs.published: This quarter is already published. Past lists are kept as they were.

mp.not_signed_in: Sign in to answer the manager pulse.
mp.forbidden: The manager pulse is answered by line managers.
mp.closed: The manager pulse is open from 15 September to 15 December.
mp.invalid: Give a whole percentage from 0 to 100, and a team size from 1 to 500 if you add one.

ht.not_signed_in: Sign in to see technologies in demand.
ht.forbidden: Only framework owners (instructors, the training manager and admins) maintain technology tags and badges.
ht.invalid: Check the technology and the quarter: one value is not accepted.
ht.source_not_found: Link a technology to an existing opportunity or role-profile version.
ht.open_quarter: Badges are published only after the quarter has ended.
ht.published: Badges for this quarter are already published. Past quarters are kept as they were.

ssg.not_signed_in: Sign in to see skills you may have.
ssg.forbidden: This step is not open to your role.
ssg.invalid: Choose confirm, reject or not me.

rs.intro: Each quarter HR publishes the skills rising across ENEC from three signals: goals set and profiles updated, recent hires holding the skill, and demand in opportunities and role profiles. Nothing is counted for a group under ten.
rs.noRuns: No quarter has been published yet.

tile.growingSub: a people signal up 25% or more

rs.nowIntro: Skills asked for most this quarter by opportunities and role profiles.
rs.growingIntro: Skills more people are working towards or bringing in than last quarter.
rs.noneNow: No skill is in demand at the published threshold this quarter.
rs.noneGrowing: No skill grew past the published threshold this quarter.
rs.noneMine: No listed skill touches your job family this quarter.
rs.howBody: Three signals, counted for the quarter and compared with the quarter before. A signal under 10 is shown as suppressed and never moves a skill.
rs.keptBody: A published list is never recomputed or edited. Pick an earlier quarter to see it exactly as it was published.
rs.hotIntro: From the same quarter's published badges.
rs.pulseBody: As a line manager you can tell HR once a year how much of your team's core skill set you expect to change by 2030.
rs.suppressedHelp: Fewer than {n}: not shown and not counted.

reason.demand: Asked for by {n} opportunities and role profiles across {families} job families this quarter.
reason.goals_profiles_new: {n} people set a goal or updated their profile for this skill; too few to count last quarter.
reason.goals_profiles_up: {n} people set a goal or updated their profile for this skill, up from {prev} ({pct}%).
reason.recent_hires_new: {n} people hired in the last year hold this skill; too few to count last quarter.
reason.recent_hires_up: {n} people hired in the last year hold this skill, up from {prev} ({pct}%).
reason.also_growing: It is also growing among people, not only in demand.

sm.intro: The published method behind ENEC Skills on the Rise, the manager pulse and the technology badges. Every number on this page is read from the same rule the list is computed with.
sm.signalsIntro: Each signal is counted for the quarter and for the quarter before.
sm.goals_profiles: Distinct staff who set a goal for the skill or recorded active evidence of it during the quarter.
sm.recent_hires: Distinct staff hired in the {days} days before the quarter ended who hold the skill.
sm.demand: Open opportunities and published role profiles (now, 2030 and 2035) that ask for the skill during the quarter.
sm.suppress: A signal under {n} is shown as suppressed, is never compared and never moves a skill.
sm.now: In demand now: demand is shown (10 or more).
sm.growing: Growing: goals and profiles or recent hires rose by {pct}% or more against the previous quarter, or appeared for the first time at 10 or more.
sm.max: At most {n} skills in each part of the list, ranked by their signals.
sm.never: Security-restricted and obsolete skills are never listed.
sm.kept: A published quarter is kept as it was; a correction is a note in the next quarter, never an overwrite.

p.quarterly: One list per ended quarter, from {first}.
p.who: An HR analyst or the HR director publishes; the training manager, admins and auditors review.
p.reasons: Every listed skill carries its reasons: which signals moved it and the job families behind the demand.

sm.pulseIntro: One question, once a year, for line managers.

pulse.who: Line managers answer between 15 September and 15 December; answering again updates the answer.
pulse.agg: HR sees the answers only as an aggregate: nothing under {n} answers, and bands and job families under {n} are suppressed.
pulse.private: No one sees an individual manager's answer.

sm.badgesIntro: Two different badges, both published per quarter.
sm.benchBody: The chips at the top of the page show the external practice this feature was compared with. They describe practice elsewhere, not a requirement.

mp.intro: One question once a year. Your answer helps HR plan learning for skills that will change; it is seen only as part of an aggregate.
mp.question: What share of your team's core skills do you expect to change by 2030?
mp.shareErr: Give a whole number from 0 to 100.
mp.teamErr: Give a whole number from 1 to 500, or leave it empty.
mp.band: Your answer is in the {lo}-{hi}% band.
mp.closedBody: It opens again on {open} and closes on {close}.
mp.privacyBody: Only you see your answer. HR sees the pulse as an aggregate of at least {n} managers, never by name.
mp.consequence: You expect {pct}% of your team's core skills to change by 2030. This is your {y} answer; you can update it until the pulse closes.

ht.intro: Generic technologies, never vendor brands. Hot across ENEC means many opportunities and role profiles in several job families ask for it; in demand for a role means your role's profile or your job family's opportunities ask for it.
ht.noBadges: No technology badges have been published yet.
ht.hotIntro: Ranked by the number of sources, then job families.
ht.noHot: No technology met the hot criteria this quarter.
ht.roleIntro: Starts on your role; pick another to compare.
ht.noRole: Choose a role to see its badges.
ht.noRoleBadges: No technology is in demand for this role this quarter.
ht.criteriaIntro: Published with each quarter's badges; the same rule computes them.

c.window: Counted over the last {n} quarters up to the end of the quarter.
c.sources: At least {n} distinct opportunities or role-profile versions tagged with it.
c.recent: At least {n} of them in the quarter itself.
c.profile: The role's published profile is tagged with it, or
c.family: at least {n} opportunities in the role's job family are tagged with it.
c.kept: Past quarters are kept as they were published.

ht.brandsBody: Technology names are generic. The catalogue refuses vendor and product names, so a badge never endorses a supplier.

reason.sources: {n} opportunities and role profiles tagged with it in the window.
reason.profile: Your role's published profile is tagged with it.
reason.family: {n} opportunities in the role's job family are tagged with it.

hta.intro: Maintain the generic technology catalogue, tag opportunities and role-profile versions, and publish the quarterly badges. Brand names are refused.
hta.readOnlyBody: You can see the catalogue and badges; framework owners make changes.

f.idHint: tech- followed by lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

problem.id: Use tech- followed by 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.
problem.name: Give a generic name of 3 to 80 characters in English and in Arabic.
problem.description: Give a description of 20 to 400 characters in English and in Arabic.
problem.brand: Use generic words only: no vendor or product brand name.
problem.skills: Up to six catalogue skills, each once.

hta.brandFound: Brand names found: {list}. Use a generic description instead.
hta.consequenceNew: The technology is added to the catalogue and can be tagged. Audited.
hta.consequenceEdit: The technology becomes version {v}. Published badges keep their quarter. Audited.
hta.noLinks: This technology is not tagged on anything yet.
hta.keptNote: This quarter is published and kept as it was.
hta.readyNote: This quarter has ended: compute the badges, review them, then publish.
hta.openNote: This quarter has not ended: you can compute a preview, but not publish.
hta.publishConsequence: The {q} badges are published to all staff and kept as they are. A published quarter cannot be changed. Audited and recorded in the ledger.

sw.intro: Compute the quarterly list for review and publish it; read the manager pulse and the skill-suggestion counts as aggregates. Never a named person.
sw.keptNote: This quarter is published and kept as it was.
sw.readyNote: This quarter has ended: compute, review and publish.
sw.openNote: This quarter has not ended: you can compute a preview, but not publish.
sw.emptyPreview: No skill reaches the list for this quarter.
sw.summaryHint: Up to 600 characters, shown with the list.
sw.publishConsequence: The {q} list is published to all staff and kept as it is. A published quarter cannot be changed. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
sw.readOnlyBody: HR analysts and the HR director publish; you can compute and review.
sw.pulseSuppressedBody: The pulse is shown only once at least ten managers have answered.
sw.pulsePrivacy: Aggregates only: nothing under {n} answers; bands and job families under {n} are suppressed.
sw.statsNote: Every count under {n} is suppressed. No person is shown.
sw.fairIntro: Weekly: the share of staff reached by suggestions by gender and nationality, suppressed under 10, flagged under four fifths of the highest group.
sw.fairConsequence: Stores this week's fairness snapshot of the suggestions surface. Audited and recorded in the ledger.

ssg.intro: Skills you may have, inferred from your own gigs, contributions, learning and the skills you already hold. Nothing is added to your profile until you confirm.
ssg.openIntro: Highest score first. Open Why this to see where each one comes from.
ssg.noneOpenBody: Refresh after new gigs, contributions or learning; answered suggestions stay below.
ssg.answeredIntro: Rejected and not me suggestions stay hidden for {n} days, then may return if still backed.
ssg.howIntro: A skill is suggested at {t} points or more, at level 2 from {l2} points; at most {n} at a time. Skills you already hold are never suggested.
ssg.never: Security-restricted and obsolete skills are never suggested. No protected attribute (such as gender, age or nationality) is an input.
ssg.privacyBody: Only you see your suggestions. Your manager does not. A confirmed suggestion becomes claimed evidence on your profile, which you can edit like any other.

rule.gig: A gig you completed listed the skill.
rule.contribution: A contribution you made is tagged with a skill related to it.
rule.xapi: Learning activity on the skill in the last {days} days: {n} refresher completions, or one other result.
rule.co_occurrence: Among staff holding a skill you hold ({holders} or more), at least {both} also hold this one, at {lift} times the usual rate or more.
rule.adjacency: Adjacent to a skill you hold; more at level 3 or above.

reason.gig: You took part in the gig {gig}.
reason.xapi: {n} learning results on this skill in the last year.
reason.co_occurrence: {pct}% of staff who hold {skill} also hold this one ({lift} times the usual rate).
reason.adjacency: Adjacent to {skill}, which you hold at level {level}.

confirm.title: Confirm {skill}
confirm.body: Adds {skill} to your profile at level {level} as claimed evidence. You can edit or remove it on My skills.

reject.title: Reject {skill}
reject.body: The suggestion is hidden for {n} days. Nothing changes on your profile.

not_me.title: Not me: {skill}
not_me.body: Tells us the suggestion does not fit you. It is hidden for {n} days and nothing changes on your profile.

done.confirm: Skill confirmed and added as claimed evidence
